claims.text: Adding titanium or vanadium can introduce controlled lattice distortion in eutectic high-entropy alloys with dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Titanium or vanadium should be added at a concentration of 2–5 at.%.
Alloying-induced lattice distortion reduces stress concentration at internal boundaries.
Reduced stress concentration at internal boundaries inhibits microcracking during room-temperature tensile deformation.
Inhibiting microcracking through lattice distortion improves yield strength.
Inhibiting microcracking through lattice distortion improves room-temperature tensile ductility.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 15–20% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The intervention will increase tensile ductility by 30–40% relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The unmodified lamellar-colony baseline has a yield strength of 800 MPa.
The unmodified lamellar-colony baseline has a tensile ductility of 10%.
Introducing new defects or impurities through alloy selection could compromise the material's properties.
Excessive lattice distortion could prevent the proposed improvement in material properties.
The optimal alloying concentration and resulting lattice distortion may vary with alloy composition and processing conditions.
